key: sensible world of soccer (1994)(renegade)[cr hlm][a](disk 1 of 2)/Sensible World of Soccer (1994)(Renegade)[cr HLM][a](Disk 1 of 2).adf:hoodlum:0:015E
name: mask_and_conditional_call
description: Ands a word from one register with a word from another, and when a byte comparison between two more registers shows the first is lower, it calls another routine and returns that routine's word instead. Otherwise it returns the masked word.

key: sensible world of soccer (1994)(renegade)[cr hlm][a](disk 1 of 2)/Sensible World of Soccer (1994)(Renegade)[cr HLM][a](Disk 1 of 2).adf:hoodlum:0:016A
name: return_empty_routine
description: Contains nothing but a return, so it changes no memory or registers. It is called from two other routines.

key: sensible world of soccer (1994)(renegade)[cr hlm][a](disk 1 of 2)/Sensible World of Soccer (1994)(Renegade)[cr HLM][a](Disk 1 of 2).adf:hoodlum:0:0182
name: build_bit_mask_table
description: Reads a count and then that many bytes from a callee into a buffer. For each value from 1 to 16 it scans the buffer and writes bit masks, shifted words and derived lengths into a table at the destination.

key: sensible world of soccer (1994)(renegade)[cr hlm][a](disk 1 of 2)/Sensible World of Soccer (1994)(Renegade)[cr HLM][a](Disk 1 of 2).adf:hoodlum:0:020A
name: accumulate_pending_list_entries
description: When the first word matches a fixed tag, it clears the tag and walks a chain of entries, zeroing each entry's fields and adding a shift-derived offset value into a target table. It also releases storage through the Exec library.

key: sensible world of soccer (1994)(renegade)[cr hlm][a](disk 1 of 2)/Sensible World of Soccer (1994)(Renegade)[cr HLM][a](Disk 1 of 2).adf:MB:0:0000
name: wait_for_port_bit_clear
description: Spins while bit six of a status value is set, then returns. The pseudo-code reads a global, but the register notes place this flag on the CIA port A line that carries the fire buttons and disk status.

name: initialise_custom_chip_registers
description: Opens a system library and, if that succeeds, configures the display window, data fetch, copper list, blitter and interrupt registers. It briefly forbids and permits task switching around the library lookup and closes the library before returning.

name: fill_four_stepped_pairs
description: Writes four pairs of 16-bit halves of a 32-bit value into a table, adding 5000 to the value after each pair.

name: fill_eight_stepped_pairs
description: Writes eight pairs of 16-bit halves of a 32-bit value into a table, adding 264 to the value after each pair.

name: run_sequenced_calls_return_third
description: Calls four routines in order and returns the result of the third call. The fourth call runs after the result is captured.

name: advance_frame_timers_and_chips
description: Once per frame it reads the DMA status and waits for the busy flag to clear, then updates frame counters and table indices using thresholds of 700 and 699. It calls about a dozen helper routines to refresh chip state and advance timers.

name: reset_blitter_and_counters
description: Waits for the blitter to go idle, then writes initial values into a blitter control block and zeroes a 24-word table of globals. It also sets a counter to 392 and resets two indices and a state value to 3.

name: step_wrapping_counters_and_reload
description: Advances a set of counters that wrap once they pass 29 and carry into a neighbouring counter, calling a helper on each step. It then copies seven words from a fixed table into the work area and clears the word after them.

name: copy_eight_words_with_stride
description: Computes a destination pointer from a counter and an index, then copies eight words from the source buffer, advancing the destination by 220 bytes between words. For indices above five it writes every word to the same location.

name: advance_position_when_flagged
description: If a flag byte in a table is set, it calls a helper, advances a column index that wraps past 29, and adds nine to a row index on each wrap. It then always calls a second helper.

name: scatter_eight_bytes_with_stride
description: Writes eight bytes from a source buffer into a destination table at a 40-byte step, after computing the destination from two counters. The source advances 66 bytes per byte written.

name: configure_blitter_dma_priority
description: Waits for the blitter to become idle, calls helpers, saves three words of a counter set, and then writes the DMA control register twice to clear and set the blitter priority and DMA enable bits.

name: update_two_arrays_by_coefficients
description: Loops over a count of entries and, for each, adds a fixed-point product of a coefficient from a third array to two arrays, scaling the product down by 1024.

name: flag_triangle_orientation_records
description: Walks a list of three-index records, computing a signed cross-product test from two coordinate tables for each record. It sets the record's flag word to one when the test passes and leaves it zero otherwise.

name: clear_blitter_control_fields
description: Waits for the blitter to be idle, then zeroes four control words, stores a long value into one control field and writes fixed values into two more control words.

name: advance_three_counters_with_wrap
description: Adds three increments to three counters and wraps each counter back by 720 when it passes 719.

name: scale_vertex_table_by_factor
description: Loads a count from a data pointer and, for each entry, multiplies two stored coordinates by a scale value into two tables and copies a third value into a third table.

name: scale_vertex_table_all_axes
description: Loads a count from a data pointer and, for each entry, multiplies three stored coordinates by a scale value and writes each result into its own table.

name: start_blit_with_fixed_addresses
description: Waits for the blitter to become idle, loads two fixed addresses into the blitter pointer fields, clears one field and writes control and size values to start the operation.

name: walk_entries_and_call_helpers
description: Waits for the blitter to be idle and sets up control fields, then walks a table of entries. For each flagged entry it runs one or both helper routines, depending on two bits of the entry's flag word.

name: setup_blitter_line_draw
description: Computes the horizontal and vertical extents of a line from two endpoints, then looks up an octant code and writes error and length values into the blitter registers. It repeats the register writes for longer lines.

name: write_blitter_block_odd_offsets
description: Waits for the blitter to be idle, then writes a fixed set of values into a control block at odd offsets, including two pointer values and a count.

name: write_blitter_block_even_offsets
description: Waits for the blitter to be idle, then writes a fixed set of values into a control block at even offsets, including two pointer values and a size field.

name: call_four_routines_in_order
description: Calls four routines in sequence and does no work of its own.

name: start_blit_with_source_pointers
description: Waits for the blitter to be idle, stores two passed-in pointer values into the blitter address registers, sets a count and writes control values to begin the operation.

name: run_four_routines_in_sequence
description: Calls four routines one after another and does no work of its own.

name: chain_four_routine_calls
description: Calls four routines in order, leaving the calls to do all the work.

name: pack_bits_into_word
description: Takes a bit from the low end of a value, combines it with an offset byte and the shifted value into a packed 32-bit word, stores that word to memory and returns the value shifted right by one. Two other routines call it.

name: read_next_table_entry_wrapping
description: Reads the next six-byte entry from a table and stores its first two words in globals. When the entry's third word is negative, the index wraps back to the start and the search repeats; otherwise the third word is stored and the index advances.

name: copy_entries_and_update_third
description: Copies 17 three-word entries into three tables and updates each source third word in place by adding twelve and its own high byte.

name: store_two_pointers_and_constants
description: Stores the low and high halves of a 32-bit value, and of that value plus 40, into four 16-bit locations. It then writes the constants 63030 and 8 to two more locations.

name: start_blit_with_shared_value
description: Waits for the blitter to be idle, clears several control fields and stores a shared value into a pointer field. It then writes control words and a size value to start the operation.

name: scale_two_arrays_by_coefficient
description: Loops over 17 entries and, for each, adds a fixed-point product of a coefficient from a third array, scaled by 64, to two arrays in place.

name: set_bitmap_bits_for_points
description: Iterates over 17 points, converting each scaled position into a bit index and setting one bit in a bitmap. Points in one depth range also set a second bit 40 bytes further on, and points outside the clip bounds are copied through unchanged.

name: store_three_fixed_constants
description: Stores the constants 710, 670 and 10 into three fixed global locations.

name: rotate_points_by_two_angles
description: Looks up coefficients for two angles from tables and rotates each stored point in fixed-point arithmetic, writing the rotated coordinates back in place.

name: initialise_audio_channel_state
description: Fills a 32-entry table with values stepping by 30, finds the largest byte in a 128-byte block and clears an area sized from it, then points 31 channel records into that area. It finally zeroes the four audio volume registers and clears several globals.

name: reload_audio_channel_pointers
description: Advances a counter by sixteen steps, and when it wraps to zero, waits and copies eight audio channel location and length values from stored table entries into the custom chip registers. Otherwise it calls one helper and updates the counter.

name: process_tracker_effect_command
description: Calls four helper routines, then reads a command from the channel row and dispatches on its nibble. Commands slide a volume or period value, step through a lookup table or set counters, and the update writes audio channel location and length registers.

name: update_channel_playback_state
description: Advances one audio channel from its pattern row, looking up a sample pointer and length from tables, updating volume and period fields, and calling helpers. It writes the channel's DMA control and location registers when a new row starts.

name: apply_channel_effect_command
description: Performs a channel's effect for one tick by reading its fields, calling helpers and dispatching on the command nibble. Commands can set speed, slide volume or pitch, set counters, or pass through a stored value.

name: find_channel_target_step
description: Searches a per-channel table for the first entry above the channel's current value, optionally stepping back one entry, and stores that entry as the target. It sets a direction flag when the target is below the current value and clears the target when it equals the current value.

name: slide_channel_value_toward_target
description: Moves a channel's current value toward its target by a per-tick step, stopping at the target and clearing it there. It then writes a table-looked-up value to the output, and does nothing when no target is set.

name: compute_phase_modulated_offset
description: Looks up a waveform table value at the channel's phase, scales it by a depth nibble, and writes the result plus the channel's base value to the output. It then advances the phase by a rate taken from the upper nibble of a parameter byte.

name: dispatch_channel_effect_command
description: Dispatches a row command by its command nibble. Commands set an effect speed, slide a volume or pitch value, set a counter or sample offset, and call helpers for the remaining cases.

name: store_low_nibble_field
description: Stores the low four bits of a source byte into a channel field at a fixed offset. The recovered code is a single store, shorter than the instruction count reported for this routine, so nothing more is described.

name: advance_wrapping_pointer_on_overflow
description: When the upper nibble of a parameter selects a non-zero table entry, it adds that entry to a counter byte. If the counter's high bit is then set, it clears the counter, advances a pointer by one byte with wrap to the buffer start, and negates the byte there.

name: load_relocatable_program
description: Copies a program name from the command argument into a buffer, appends a relocation file extension and opens the file through the DOS library. It then sets up interrupt and DMA registers, applies relocation entries and jumps into the loaded program. If opening fails it shows an error message and loops forever.

name: apply_relocations_and_enter
description: Applies relocation additions to a list of longword offsets within a loaded block, then transfers control to the block's entry through a computed address. For an unsupported block kind it shows an error message and loops forever.

name: copy_bytes_then_jump
description: Copies a block of bytes from a source to a destination for a given count, then jumps to the address held in a computed pointer.

name: copy_bytes_backwards_then_jump
description: Copies a block of bytes from its end toward its start, so overlapping regions move safely, then jumps through a computed pointer. Its referenced text is a set of loader error messages.

name: print_text_via_library
description: Opens a library, measures a NUL-terminated text argument, and then calls two library functions with it. It uses the same library calls as the loader's error-reporting path.

name: probe_memory_regions_by_type
description: Probes 32 memory regions by calling the Exec library's memory type function at a series of addresses. For each region it records whether memory was found, whether a type flag bit is set, and the total size found, storing the bit masks and size in globals.

name: allocate_memory_block
description: Allocates memory through the Exec library's allocation call and calls one other routine. The decompiler timed out, so the allocation details are not described further.
